# Install {#admin-install}

Kailash ships bootable images in two formats per profile: a **QEMU
disk image** (the primary deliverable shape) and a **bootable ISO**.
Each image is a row of one declared table — every flake attribute,
size budget, CI leg and release asset name derives from that single
declaration, and a check leg fails CI if a table row loses its build
surface, so the download list cannot silently drift.

## The image matrix

| Ref (`nix build .#<ref>`) | Profile | Format | System | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kailash-images-qemu-minimal` | minimal | qcow2 | x86_64 | ≤4 GB |
| `kailash-images-iso-minimal` | minimal | ISO | x86_64 | ≤4 GB |
| `kailash-images-qemu-redteam-ai` | redteam-ai | qcow2 | x86_64 | ≤8 GB |
| `kailash-images-iso-redteam-ai` | redteam-ai | ISO | x86_64 | ≤8 GB |
| `kailash-images-qemu-full` | full | qcow2 | x86_64 | ≤10 GB |
| `kailash-images-iso-full` | full | ISO | x86_64 | ≤10 GB |
| `kailash-images-qemu-headless-agent` | headless-agent | qcow2 | x86_64 | ≤1.5 GB |
| `kailash-images-iso-headless-agent` | headless-agent | ISO | x86_64 | ≤1.5 GB |
| `kailash-images-qemu-aarch64-minimal` | minimal | qcow2 | aarch64 | ≤4 GB |
| `kailash-images-iso-aarch64-minimal` | minimal | ISO | aarch64 | ≤4 GB |
| `kailash-images-qemu-aarch64-headless-agent` | headless-agent | qcow2 | aarch64 | ≤1.5 GB |
| `kailash-images-iso-aarch64-headless-agent` | headless-agent | ISO | aarch64 | ≤1.5 GB |

x86_64 images are built by hosted CI; aarch64 rows are built on the
project's Apple Silicon builder. The `aarch64` `redteam-ai` rows are
the newest slice of the matrix (tracked on the OS repository's issue
tracker — the table above reflects the declared matrix, which is the
truth CI holds images to).

## Getting an image

Release assets (per the release's SHA256SUMS sheet, mirrored to the
main site), then verify the checksum before first boot — the release
notes name where the sums sheet and validator output are recorded.
The size budgets are enforced by construction: heavy data packs
(texlive, gnuradio, wordlist/SDR corpora) never enter a default
image — they ride opt-in `kailash-data.*` derivations, which is why
the `full` image stays inside its budget.
